title: Building a web page with HTML
examples: What is the difference between a heading and a paragraph?
How do I make a picture appear on my webpage?
Can I link to another website using HTML?

explain.say: Today we learn about HTML to build web pages.

draw.text: Building a web page with HTML

explain.say: Tags are like instructions for the web browser.
Headings help show the most important titles on your page.
Paragraphs group blocks of regular text together nicely.
Links let you connect your page to another web page.
Images let you put pictures onto your webpage easily.

faq.q: What is the difference between an h1 and an h2?
faq.a: An h1 is for the main title of the whole page. An h2 is for a major section title underneath the main title.
asks: Should I use h1 for every section?

faq.q: Why do I need to close my tags?
faq.a:
You must close tags like this:

so the browser knows where the instruction ends. If you forget it, the page layout might break.
asks: What happens if I forget a closing tag?
Do all tags need a closing tag?

faq.q: What do I put in the href attribute for a link?
faq.a: The href stands for hyperlink reference. You put the full web address, like http://example.com, inside the quotes.
asks: Where do I find the web address?
Is it the whole website address I need?

faq.q: Can I use an image tag without a source?
faq.a: No, the image tag needs a source attribute, which tells the browser exactly where the picture file is located. Otherwise, nothing will show up.
asks: What is the src for an image?
Does the picture need a file path?

faq.q: If I want a title that is smaller than h2, what should I use?
faq.a: You should use the next heading tag down, which is h3. The tags go from h1 down to h6 in order of size.
asks: What is the next heading after h2?
How many heading levels are there?

facts: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language.
Tags are used to structure content on a webpage.
The <h1> tag creates the most important heading.
The <a> tag is used specifically for creating hyperlinks.

quiz.say: To make a title that is smaller than the main page title, which tag should you use?
quiz.why: h2 is the correct tag because it represents a secondary, but still important, section heading.

wrong.0: A paragraph tag is for regular text blocks, not for section titles.
wrong.1: This is the largest heading and should be reserved for the primary page title.
wrong.3: h1 is too big; it should only be used for the main title of the entire page.

quiz.say: Which tag must you use to make text clickable and link to another page?
quiz.why: The anchor tag, <a>, is specifically designed to create hyperlinks between web pages.

wrong.0: There is no standard <url> tag in HTML for creating links.
wrong.2: The <link> tag is used differently, often for connecting stylesheets, not for clickable text.
wrong.3: href is an attribute, not a tag itself, so it cannot wrap the text.

quiz.say: If you want to display a picture named 'sunset.jpg' from the 'images' folder, what attribute must you use?
quiz.why: The src attribute inside the tag tells the browser the exact source path of the image file.

wrong.0: alt is for the alternative text, which describes the image, not the path.
wrong.1: This might work if the image is in the same folder, but it misses the required 'images/' folder path.
wrong.2: The correct attribute name for the source is 'src', not 'file'.
